title.en: Segmentation labels: overlap and reference-grid conversion

summary: Validate categorical segment identity, overlapping membership and target-grid geometry before exporting a segmentation.
objective: Export a segmentation with overlapping regions to a target grid and expose any lost membership, cropped extent or changed representation.
intent_signals: Export a segmentation with overlapping regions to a target grid and expose any lost membership, cropped extent or changed representation.
example_prompts: Export a segmentation with overlapping regions to a target grid and expose any lost membership, cropped extent or changed representation.
applies_when: Validate categorical segment identity, overlapping membership and target-grid geometry before exporting a segmentation.

principles: Separate segment identity and membership from label values, colors and derived surface meshes. A smooth surface is a representation choice, not a replacement source segmentation.
Treat label resampling and merged-label export as declared conversions with their own loss report. Visual alignment alone does not establish matching spatial frames.
implementation: Record source segment IDs/names, reference volume revision, origin, spacing, axis directions and extents. Resolve parent transforms into a shared patient/model frame before comparing grids; do not equate equal array dimensions with equal geometry.

Preserve separate binary memberships or a representation supporting overlap. If a target requires one label per voxel, require and disclose an explicit overlap-resolution policy instead of silently overwriting segments.

For categorical resampling choose an explicit label-preserving method such as nearest-neighbor; document that this avoids interpolated label numbers but can still erase thin regions. Record derived-surface smoothing and conversion parameters separately.
Before export report target-extent cropping, dropped segment IDs and changed membership counts. Keep the original segmentation unchanged and expose source versus converted views at the same location.
observable_checks: Use two synthetic masks sharing one voxel: source inspection reports membership in both; merged-label export either rejects the overlap or records which membership the chosen policy removes.
Use equal-sized grids with different origins, then a target extent that excludes a labeled voxel: detect misalignment and report cropping, not successful lossless export.
Resample labels {0,3,8}; output introduces no invented labels such as 4 or 5. Compare thin-region survival and review any change rather than treating label validity as full fidelity.

known_limits: Does not certify anatomical correctness, lesion boundaries or clinical measurements. Fractional/probabilistic segmentation needs a separate explicit policy.
Authored source-reviewed guidance only; no import adapter, runtime artifact or scientific pipeline was implemented or executed.
creative_affordances: Use a compact source-versus-display inspector to expose the specific transformation; layout and emphasis are authored choices, not validated usability findings.

claims.statement: Slicer supports multiple representations per segment, preserves overlapping segmentation data using additional volume layers, and warns that exporting to a reference volume can crop regions outside its geometry.
claims.scope: Documented Slicer representation/export behavior; proposed categorical validation procedures are authored.
